title: CA-GPT, a DeepSeek-based model on an AI-OCT system led by Tangdu Hospital, agrees with expert PCI plans more than ChatGPT-5 and junior physicians in a 96-patient single-center preprint
summary: In a 96-patient preprint, CA-GPT matched expert stent plans more often. It processed raw OCT images, while ChatGPT-5 received extracted measurements, limiting the model comparison.
account: An arXiv preprint of 11 December 2025 (Fang et al., last author Yan Li) reports the single-center COMPARE study. It compared CA-GPT, “a novel large model deployed on an AI-OCT system”, with ChatGPT-5 and junior physicians. This was in optical coherence tomography (OCT)-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Decisions for 96 patients were scored against an expert-derived record. In pre-PCI planning CA-GPT's median agreement was 5 against 3 for ChatGPT-5 and 4 for junior physicians. It “showed superior performance to junior physicians in stent diameter (90.3% vs. 72.2%, P<0.05) and length selection (80.6% vs. 52.8%, P<0.01)”. Machine Heart (Sina, 16 December 2025) says Li Yan's team at Tangdu Hospital and Zhu Rui's at Shenzhen Tsinghua University Research Institute built it. They used open-source DeepSeek with retrieval over a million cardiovascular papers, on a Vivolight OCT platform. The Monitor pairs this study with a Xinhua report (13 December 2025) on the “Titian” ablation robot at Shaoxing People's Hospital. It describes teleoperation and no AI function. The original Methods describe retrieval from more than 100,000 annotated PCI cases and clinical guidance. That description differs from the press account’s claim of a million cardiovascular papers. CA-GPT received raw OCT images through its integrated pipeline, whereas ChatGPT-5 received manually extracted measurements. The comparison therefore combines differences in models, retrieval, and input processing.
purpose: CA-GPT was built to interpret intravascular OCT images and generate PCI planning and assessment decisions as expert-level support. The reported agreement with expert records is that purpose.
system: CA-GPT large model on an AI-OCT system (COMPARE study)
model_version: CA-GPT built on open-source DeepSeek with retrieval-augmented generation over more than one million cardiovascular papers and guidelines, per Machine Heart; version not stated
developer: Tangdu Hospital, Air Force Medical University (Li Yan's team) with Shenzhen Tsinghua University Research Institute (Zhu Rui's team), on a Vivolight Medtech OCT platform
deployer: Tangdu Hospital, Air Force Medical University (study lead, per Machine Heart)

ratings.reason: A single-center preprint comparing decision agreement. No patient outcome, deployment or event is reported.

ai_role.statement: CA-GPT is the system under test: a large model on an AI-OCT platform producing pre- and post-PCI decisions that were scored against an expert record. Its reported advantage over ChatGPT-5 and junior physicians is the authors' own measurement in a preprint that has not been peer reviewed. The decisions were not acted on for the 96 patients.

fields.account: An arXiv preprint of 11 December 2025 (Fang et al., last author Yan Li) reports the single-center COMPARE study. It compared CA-GPT, “a novel large model deployed on an AI-OCT system”, with ChatGPT-5 and junior physicians. This was in optical coherence tomography (OCT)-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Decisions for 96 patients were scored against an expert-derived record. In pre-PCI planning CA-GPT's median agreement was 5 against 3 for ChatGPT-5 and 4 for junior physicians. It “showed superior performance to junior physicians in stent diameter (90.3% vs. 72.2%, P<0.05) and length selection (80.6% vs. 52.8%, P<0.01)”. Machine Heart (Sina, 16 December 2025) says Li Yan's team at Tangdu Hospital and Zhu Rui's at Shenzhen Tsinghua University Research Institute built it. They used open-source DeepSeek with retrieval over a million cardiovascular papers, on a Vivolight OCT platform. The Monitor pairs this study with a Xinhua report (13 December 2025) on the “Titian” ablation robot at Shaoxing People's Hospital. It describes teleoperation and no AI function. The original Methods describe retrieval from more than 100,000 annotated PCI cases and clinical guidance. That description differs from the press account’s claim of a million cardiovascular papers. CA-GPT received raw OCT images through its integrated pipeline, whereas ChatGPT-5 received manually extracted measurements. The comparison therefore combines differences in models, retrieval, and input processing.

fields.summary: In a 96-patient preprint, CA-GPT matched expert stent plans more often. It processed raw OCT images, while ChatGPT-5 received extracted measurements, limiting the model comparison.
fields.account: An arXiv preprint of 11 December 2025 (Fang et al., last author Yan Li) reports the single-center COMPARE study. It compared CA-GPT, “a novel large model deployed on an AI-OCT system”, with ChatGPT-5 and junior physicians. This was in optical coherence tomography (OCT)-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Decisions for 96 patients were scored against an expert-derived record. In pre-PCI planning CA-GPT's median agreement was 5 against 3 for ChatGPT-5 and 4 for junior physicians. It “showed superior performance to junior physicians in stent diameter (90.3% vs. 72.2%, P<0.05) and length selection (80.6% vs. 52.8%, P<0.01)”. Machine Heart (Sina, 16 December 2025) says Li Yan's team at Tangdu Hospital and Zhu Rui's at Shenzhen Tsinghua University Research Institute built it. They used open-source DeepSeek with retrieval over a million cardiovascular papers, on a Vivolight OCT platform. The Monitor pairs this study with a Xinhua report (13 December 2025) on the “Titian” ablation robot at Shaoxing People's Hospital. It describes teleoperation and no AI function. The original Methods describe retrieval from more than 100,000 annotated PCI cases and clinical guidance. That description differs from the press account’s claim of a million cardiovascular papers. CA-GPT received raw OCT images through its integrated pipeline, whereas ChatGPT-5 received manually extracted measurements. The comparison therefore combines differences in models, retrieval, and input processing.
